name: laravel
label: Laravel application
description: A door into a Laravel application that has benjaminledel/covey-laravel installed: the schema and read-only SQL behind the read token, tinker (PHP in the application's context) behind the write token.

schema.doc: the tables of the application's database (hidden tables left out); no params

columns.doc: the columns of one table with type, nullable and default; params: table

query.doc: ONE read-only SQL statement (SELECT/WITH/SHOW/EXPLAIN), rows capped; params: sql, bindings (optional array for ? placeholders), limit (optional). Anything that writes is refused here — that is tinker.

tinker.subject: laravel:tinker
tinker.doc: run PHP in the application's context, as `php artisan tinker` would (Eloquent, facades, jobs); params: code. This CHANGES things: say in one line what and why before you call it, and never call it for something query can answer.

prompt_doc: This Laravel application is reachable through four actions. Read first: schema and columns tell you the tables, query runs one SELECT with a row cap and strips columns the application hides. tinker is the only way to change anything and is governed separately — an organisation may require an approval for it, and an agent that only holds the read token does not have it at all. Prefer query over tinker for every question; use tinker for a change you were asked to make, name the record you touch, and read it back afterwards.
